title: Luxury wedding venues around the world: a global guide
seo_title: Luxury wedding venues: global guide to costs and booking
dek: Discover how to select luxury wedding venues that offer exceptional service and design, from beachfront resorts in Dubai to tropical estates in Bali.
body:
Selecting the right setting is the most significant decision in your planning process, often accounting for over half of a total budget. While luxury is frequently associated with a high price point, it is defined more accurately by the quality of service, the beauty of the architecture and the ability to create a personalised experience. Whether you are looking for an intimate garden or a grand ballroom, the world's most sought-after locations provide the foundation for a celebration that reflects your specific style.

## Defining the luxury wedding experience

Luxury is a standard of excellence rather than a specific price bracket. Savills research indicates that the most sought-after locations are those that are architecturally beautiful and easy to decorate, allowing you to create a celebration that feels authentic to your story. According to Savills, 31% of couples say that an outside space is what sets their chosen location apart from others.

### Service and personalisation
A hallmark of a premium venue is the level of service and attention to detail. This often includes expert wedding specialists who manage every element, from the initial enquiry to the final departure. High-end establishments, such as the St. Regis Downtown Dubai, provide bespoke services like a dedicated butler and flexible check-in times for the couple. Modern luxury is experience-led, moving away from rigid formats in favour of personalised touches. This might involve a traditional Abra boat arrival at a waterfront location like the Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri in Abu Dhabi or a private photoshoot on a secluded beach.

### Essential facilities for luxury wedding venues
Practical luxury often manifests in the facilities provided for preparation. Savills notes a growing demand for dedicated spaces to get ready on-site. Premium locations provide private suites, such as those at Raffles Dubai, which can offer opulent settings alongside lush, serene gardens for alfresco gatherings. When researching, it is helpful to have a list of [questions to ask a wedding venue](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) regarding their specific service standards and preparation areas.

Whether the setting is a Swarovski-chandeliered ballroom or 65 acres of landscaped gardens at the One&Only Royal Mirage, the focus remains on quality. Transparency is also a key feature of the market; Savills reports that 72% of couples will not contact a venue unless clear pricing is available online.

## Iconic luxury wedding venues in the Middle East

The Middle East has become a global centre for **luxury wedding venues**, offering a mix of modern architectural feats and traditional Arabian hospitality. In cities like Dubai and Abu Dhabi, the standard of service often includes dedicated butler teams and arrival options by traditional boat or helicopter.

### Dubai city and beachfront landmarks
At Raffles Dubai, located adjacent to Wafi Mall, the setting combines an Egyptian aesthetic with Asian style. You can choose between an opulent celebration in the Swarovski-chandeliered ballroom or a quiet gathering in the gardens. The hotel offers bespoke packages, such as Raffles Enchanted Moments, which are tailored to the scale of the event.

For those seeking views of the Burj Khalifa and the Dubai Water Canal, the St. Regis Downtown Dubai offers the St. Regis Ballroom with a capacity for 350 guests. As of 2025, the hotel provides a Love Package starting at a minimum spend of Dh350 per person and an Adore Package from Dh400 per person. Both include a complimentary two-layer cake and a stay for the couple.

If you prefer a private coastline, One&Only Royal Mirage is set within 65 acres of gardens. Its outdoor Amphitheatre can host 300 guests with a minimum spend of Dh120,000, while the Peregrine Ballroom suits groups of up to 120 with a minimum spend of Dh80,000. For a more casual atmosphere, you can [discover venues on Roko](/wedding-vendors) that offer food truck catering or informal beachfront settings.

### Abu Dhabi and upcoming developments
The Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri in Abu Dhabi provides views of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque. Packages here start at Dh290 per person and can include a traditional Abra arrival for the couple, a private photoshoot on the beach and a choice between a customised cake or a bridal spa treatment.

Looking ahead to late 2027, Wynn Al Marjan Island in Ras Al Khaimah is preparing to host large-scale destination events. Its Coral Court centre will feature a Grand Ballroom for 1,260 guests and an Event Lawn for 620. A specific feature of this development is the provision of separate 150 square metre suites for the bride and groom. The Bridal Suite includes specialised studio lighting for photography, while the Groom's Suite features a cigar lounge and bar.

When comparing these locations, it is useful to prepare a list of [questions to ask a wedding venue](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) regarding minimum spend and what is included in the base price.

## Tropical elegance and destination planning in Bali

Bali provides a versatile range of luxury wedding venues that cater to different aesthetics, from the dramatic clifftops of the south to the serene jungles of the interior. When selecting a location, consider the atmosphere you wish to create and the practical needs of your guests.

### Key regions for luxury venues
*   **Uluwatu**: This area is favoured for its ocean views and is ideal for sunset ceremonies on clifftops.
*   **Ubud**: For those seeking tropical vegetation and a peaceful environment, Ubud offers venues set among rainforests and rice farms.
*   **Nusa Dua**: This region is a primary choice for upscale beach resorts and high-end accommodation.
*   **Seminyak and Jimbaran**: These areas provide easy access to stylish nightlife and classic beach settings.

### The benefit of local expertise
Hiring a local wedding planner is a strategic move for destination celebrations. According to Luxury Travel Magazine, a local expert can help you compare wedding packages, coordinate with florists and photographers, and manage local arrangements that might be difficult to handle from abroad. They can also ensure the planning happens in phases to reduce pressure and help you find venues that fit your specific price range.

When researching, it is helpful to have a list of [questions to ask a wedding venue](/journal/questions-to-ask-a-wedding-venue) before you book, particularly regarding accessibility. Remote clifftop locations may offer incredible views but can present travel challenges for older guests compared to a resort where everyone stays on-site.

### Practical considerations
Always ask about indoor or covered alternatives for rainy days and specific rules regarding music, entertainment or event times. When reviewing costs, compare complete quotes rather than just the advertised base price. A venue with a lower initial fee might lack essential services, leading to higher overall spending. You can [discover event specialists](/wedding-vendors) through Roko to assist with these specific requirements.

## The rise of multi-day and cultural celebrations

Modern luxury is increasingly defined by the duration and depth of the experience. Savills research indicates a growing demand for destination-style venues that support two-day or weekend-long celebrations, moving away from rigid, one-day packages. This shift is particularly evident in the planning of cultural weddings, which often require specific architectural layouts and specialised hospitality services.

### Facilities for traditional ceremonies
Venues are now being designed with the specific requirements of Indian and Pakistani celebrations in mind. In the UAE, the upcoming Wynn Al Marjan Island, scheduled to open in late 2027, includes dedicated spaces for traditional events such as the Haldi, Mehndi, Sangeet and Baraat. These celebrations often involve separate preparation areas for the couple. The resort plans to offer 150 square metre suites for both the bride and groom; the bridal suite features specialised studio lighting for photography and makeup, while the groom's suite includes a private cigar lounge and bar.

When browsing [wedding vendors](/wedding-vendors) on Roko, look for venues that offer specific cultural accommodations:

*   **Privacy and gender-separation:** Dedicated arrival routes and the option for gender-separated celebrations, as seen at Coral Court in Ras Al Khaimah.
*   **Specialised catering:** Culinary teams capable of producing authentic Indian, Arabic or Jain menus, or venues that allow external food trucks for informal evening options.
*   **Arrival experiences:** Features like the traditional Abra boat arrival at the Shangri-La Qaryat Al Beri in Abu Dhabi or helicopter and yacht arrivals at JA The Resort.

### Investment in multi-day events
According to 2026 figures from Asian Wedding Experts cited by Which?, an Indian Hindu wedding in the UK typically costs between £38,000 and £85,000. Pakistani Muslim weddings in the same market usually range from £40,000 to £90,000. These figures reflect the scale of events that can span several days and involve multiple outfit changes, such as traditional caftans and the use of Amariya chairs. To understand how these figures compare to broader market trends, you can explore Roko's analysis of [weddings by the numbers](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show).

Venues that cater to these needs often provide an expert team to manage every detail, from bespoke 15-tier wedding cakes to coordinating multi-day itineraries across ballrooms, beach clubs and private gardens. This level of service ensures that the celebration remains a personal reflection of the couple's story, regardless of the guest count.

## Understanding the investment and venue costs

In the current market, venue hire and catering are the most significant expenses, typically accounting for 51% of total wedding spending according to a 2026 Which? report. While many smaller celebrations cost between £5,000 and £10,000, Savills research indicates that 25% of couples spend more than £26,000 on their event.

### Breaking down the budget
The cost of hosting has increased even as guest lists have become more intimate. In 2025, the average cost per guest rose to £272. This figure covers the essential elements of the day, with specific allocations often following this pattern:

*   Venue hire and catering: 51%
*   Wedding attire: 19%
*   Photography and videography: 10%
*   Decor and entertainment: 7%

Catering alone averages £5,406, with an additional £2,002 typically spent on evening snacks. When reviewing luxury wedding venues, you should also factor in hidden costs such as corkage fees, which often range from £15 for wine to £30 for champagne.

### The importance of pricing transparency
Transparency is a priority for modern planners. Savills data shows that 72% of couples will not contact a venue unless clear pricing is available online. This shift has led many premium locations to provide detailed digital brochures or upfront package costs to build trust early in the process. You can discover venues on Roko that provide this level of clarity to help you stay within your established budget.

If you are beginning your search, [Roko's analysis of official statistics](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show) provides further context on how couples are allocating their funds. Understanding these benchmarks allows you to negotiate effectively and prioritise the elements that define your personal standard of quality.

## How to secure your chosen location

Securing luxury wedding venues requires a balance of quick decision-making and thorough vetting. Research from Savills shows that 4 in 5 couples book their venue within a month of their first contact. Transparency is a significant factor in this process, as 72% of couples will not contact a venue unless clear pricing is available online.

### Booking luxury wedding venues
Competition for specific dates is high, particularly during peak seasons. In the UK, August is the most popular month for weddings, representing 17% of bookings, followed by May at 13% and September at 12%. Australian Bureau of Statistics data for 2025 shows a similar preference for specific windows, with 25 October 2025 being the most popular date of the year. Saturdays remain the most frequent choice globally, though Friday is the second most common day for weddings in Australia. You can find more details on these trends in Roko's guide to [weddings by the numbers](/journal/weddings-by-the-numbers-what-official-statistics-show).

> Budget sensitivity remains a key market feature, contributing to growth in midweek weddings, off-peak and smaller guest numbers.
> **Adam Davies**, Savills Tourism, Leisure and Events

faq.q: What is the average cost per guest at a luxury venue?
faq.a: Based on 2025 data, the cost per guest in the UK has risen to £272. In the UAE, luxury packages often start between Dh290 and Dh400 per person, depending on the venue and inclusions.

faq.q: Which months are most popular for booking luxury venues?
faq.a: Data from 2025 shows that 40% of bookings occur during peak periods from May to August. August is the most popular month at 17%, followed by May and September.

faq.q: Are multi-day weddings common at luxury resorts?
faq.a: Yes, demand for destination-style, weekend-long celebrations is increasing. Many luxury venues now offer specific facilities for multi-day events, such as traditional Indian ceremonies like Sangeet and Mehndi.
